definition: On the subject of; concerning.
example: This book is about a brave knight and a dragon.
note: Cleaned the translations. Spanish 'acerca de' and French 'à propos' are stiff; the everyday word for a book about something is 'sobre' / 'sur'. Italian was a list of grammar forms, replaced with the single word 'su'.

definition: In or to a higher position than something else.
example: The birds flew high above the tall trees.
note: Italian was a list of grammar contractions (su/sul/sulla/sullo). Replaced with the single clean word 'sopra'.

definition: The details of where someone lives or where a building is, used for sending letters.
example: Please write your name and address on the envelope.
note: The whole word had been pushed onto a rare meaning ('the president will address the nation'). The first meaning of 'address' for any learner is where you live. Example, definition and all four translations rewritten around that.

definition: The most important city of a country, where the government is based.
example: Paris is the capital of France.
note: The example sentence was broken ('Paris is the capital of France, and largest city in, France.'). Rewritten as one clean sentence.

definition: Not dirty; free from dirt and marks.
example: Please keep your room clean and tidy.
note: Had been turned into the action 'to clean'. The first meaning of 'clean' is the opposite of dirty, which is also what the original list intended. Switched back to the describing word.

definition: The activity of preparing and heating food to eat.
example: She enjoys cooking delicious meals for her family every day.
note: The four languages did not match each other: Spanish gave a half-finished form and French gave the word for a kitchen. All four now express the same idea, the act of cooking.

definition: Right; with no mistakes.
example: Your answer is correct, well done.
note: Had been turned into the action 'to correct someone's mistakes'. The first meaning of 'correct' is simply 'right', which is what the original list intended. Switched back.

definition: To make a picture using a pen or pencil.
example: She likes to draw animals with a pencil.
note: The example contained two unrelated sentences and a second, confusing meaning ('draw the curtains'). Reduced to one clear sentence.

definition: Used to stress that something is surprising or extreme.
example: Even the youngest child understood the story.
note: Had been pushed onto the rare meaning 'flat, with no bumps'. By far the most common use of 'even' is for emphasis, and that is what the original French translation showed. Rebuilt around that meaning.

definition: Having too much flesh on the body; not thin.
example: The cat is very fat because it eats too much.
note: Had been turned into the food substance (cooking fat). The first meaning of 'fat' is describing a person or animal, which is what the original German and French translations showed. Switched back.

definition: Good, well, or acceptable.
example: How are you today? I feel fine, thank you.
note: The example was two separate sentences stuck together. Reduced to one natural exchange. Italian capital letter removed.

definition: Starting at a particular place, person, or time.
example: The train arrived from London at six o'clock.
note: French 'depuis' means 'since' and is about time, not origin. The word for coming from a place is 'de'.

definition: Used to refer to a woman or girl already mentioned.
example: I saw her at the park yesterday afternoon.
note: German was three alternatives separated by slashes and Spanish used a longer phrase. All four now give the single matching word.

definition: A period of time away from work or school, often spent travelling.
example: We are going on holiday to Spain next summer.
note: All four languages had been changed to mean a public holiday because the old example was about a family dinner. The first meaning of 'holiday' is a break away from work. Example rewritten and all four translations restored.

definition: To become a member of a group, club, or organisation.
example: She wants to join the football club at school.
note: Had been pushed onto the meaning 'glue two pieces of wood together'. The first meaning of 'join' is joining a group, which is what three of the four original translations showed. Rebuilt around that.

definition: A very short time ago.
example: I just finished my homework a moment ago.
note: Italian capital letter removed.

definition: Coming after all the others; final or most recent.
example: This is the last piece of cake.
note: Had been turned into 'to go on for a period of time' ('the film will last two hours'). The first meaning of 'last' is final or most recent, which is what the original German and French showed. Rebuilt around that.

definition: The brightness that lets us see things.
example: Please turn on the light, it is dark in here.
note: All four languages had been changed to mean 'not heavy'. Every original translation was the word for brightness, and that is the first meaning of 'light'. Fully restored.

definition: The fifth month of the year.
example: My birthday is in May every year.
note: The definition and all four translations were the month, but the example was about the word 'may' meaning possibility. Example rewritten to match the month. Italian capital letter removed, as Italian months are written in lower case.

definition: Reports of recent events shared on TV, radio, or online.
example: The news reported a big storm coming our way.
note: Italian 'notiziario' is the name of a news programme rather than the news itself. Changed to 'notizie'.

definition: Away from the inside of a place.
example: She stepped out of the car quickly.
note: The example was broken ('out of the car quickly moving car'). Rewritten as one clean sentence.

definition: The time before now.
example: In the past, people travelled by horse.
note: The definition described 'the past' as a thing but the translations had been switched to describing words, so they no longer matched. Set to the thing, which is the first meaning and which all four languages share.

definition: A single idea or opinion in a discussion.
example: She made an important point during the meeting.
note: Had been pushed onto 'the sharp tip of a pen'. That is a rare use. The original translations were all the same simple word for a point or dot, so the entry now teaches the everyday meaning.

definition: The system for sending letters and parcels; the mail.
example: I sent the letter by post yesterday.
note: Had been pushed onto 'a wooden pole in the ground'. Every original translation was the word for mail, which is the first meaning of 'post'. Fully restored.

definition: The unit of money used in the United Kingdom.
example: The book costs ten pounds in the shop.
note: Had been turned into the action 'to hit something hard'. Every original translation was the unit of pound, and money is the first thing a learner meets. Rebuilt around British money.

definition: Regular activity done in order to improve a skill.
example: With enough practice, you will speak English well.
note: In British English 'practice' is the thing and 'practise' is the action, and the list has both as separate entries. Both had been made into the action, so they were identical. This one is now the thing.
